docks._doc: tools/inn_pier.py (Publisher 20 Oct, Matt's photograph): the Bar Harbor Inn pier. The fixed walkway, its piles and the booth are a landmark (landmarks.json bar_harbor_inn_pier); here the aluminium gangway from its end (lidar: 20 m, falling north), the float in line beyond it and the schooner float across its end, running east. The id is the old one: the "off-the-float" scenario names it.

docks._doc: Matt, 18 Oct: the downtown floats and the ramps down to them, traced from his aerial (Apple Maps, north up) and georeferenced to level metres on five OSM pier points (residual <= 3 m; tools/assets/aerial/trace.py). Everything a boat lies against is a float; anything coming off a float to a fixed structure is a ramp (free hinge: hinge [x, z], hinge_navd_m, dir_deg = direction down the ramp, atan2(dx, dz)). The whale-watch gangways run parallel to their floats and land mid-float. Floats are hand-placed (at = the first module's centre, heading along the run), split into ~12 m modules, each run held by four pilings on its first module (hoops 0.15 and 0.85, both sides); the whole run is one body that rides the tide. Hinge heights are +4.5 m NAVD everywhere until World checks them against its decks. replaces_osm: the OSM pier ids World draws today as fixed piers here.

docks._doc: The whale-watch floats and their gangways (moved out of bar_harbor_downtown_floats, 30 Oct, so they can look like themselves). Matt's photo from the head of the slips, 30 Oct (Friendship V port side to ww_e, a second catamaran between ww_e and ww_e2): concrete floats painted with light grey non-skid, black rub rails, black cleats, flush round yellow deck plates, short yellow bollards, a dark red line along the outer edge, a hose reel and life ring at the gangway foot, steel piles with a yellow collar at deck level, coiled lines on deck. look: the deck and the float sides are the repo's concrete_pavement (non-skid grit) tinted to the sunlit deck in the photo (#bab7b0: median of two 40 x 40 px patches of the sunlit float deck; docs/waterfront-photos.md); no planks (one board spans the float); dressing none until Assets' whale-watch dressing (requests.md). The slips are 3 m wider each than the aerial trace (Matt).

docks._doc: tools/waterfront_kit.py: the waterfront kit (docs/docks.md) placed from the chart. world.js makes the platform solid (deck box, pile cylinders).

Harbor Place, Bar Harbor: the whole fixed waterfront from the whale-watch slip head to the inlet wall, built on piles (Matt 31 Oct: "the whole of Harbor Place is also built on pilings (there is no actual ground around at all)"). Generated by tools/assets/harbor_place/dock_json.py from layout.json (docs/harbor-place.md items 1 and 4). Coordinates are LEVEL metres (x east, z south): each platform has its own at/heading, the walls are paths in level metres with at [0,0]. Floats and gangways are NOT here: they stay in levels/downeast/docks.json bar_harbor_whale_watch, hinged on this deck at +3.3. The only ground is the beach between the timber deck and Stewman's; everything under these decks is water and mud (World cuts the terrain).

docks._doc: Site 1 item 21 (docs/sites/bar-harbor-waterfront.md, rows 4.08, 4.09, 4.16). Level metres. The Harborside point's seawall and the former Golden Anchor pier under the pavilion. Wall line: chart SLCONS 4.09, moved landward to the face the 2021 lidar shows (0.5 m on the west, north and east faces, 1.2 m on the south stretch). Coping +3.9 then +3.5; rail tops +4.93 and +4.53 [lidar]; feet from the lidar on the beach, from detail.png under water. Dry granite with granite posts (Matt's photos 18 Oct, docs/docks.md) and a cream rail (photo_aerial_town_autumn.jpg). ASSUMED until V4.1: dry-laid rather than mortared, 3.6 m post pitch. Pier: 21.7 m wide, 50 m from the fill to the seaward end, deck +3.3 (the lidar's neck; the survey's +4.9 was not a deck). The building's roof covers the outer 32 m. Timber piles ASSUMED; nothing published describes them. Dressing (item 20b): authored, level metres. Seven twin-arm lamps on the east lawn from the autumn aerial: count and line seen, shape and exact spots ASSUMED until V4.1. Rail damage, the broken post, fallen stones, signs and their wording, the old piles and iron beside the pier: ASSUMED, chosen for interest; no photo shows them. Beds under the old piles from detail.png.

Site 1 item 22 (docs/sites/bar-harbor-waterfront.md, rows 3.10, 3.15, 3.16). Level metres. The Bar Harbor Club's wall and deck, the cove's curved back wall, the Harborside's west wall as far as harborside_point.json's first point. Faces, feet and tops from the 2021 lidar. Stone, rail form and the dressing are ASSUMED until V3.3.

Site 1 item 23 (docs/sites/bar-harbor-waterfront.md, stretch 5). Level metres. The Inn's seawall round its point and Grant Park's, poured in 2024-25 (VIA; Bar Harbor Inn). Faces, feet and tops: 2021 lidar (tools/assets/sites/wall_profile.py), so pre-storm positions; parapet 0.35 m over the old ground. Form, coping, footing and rail from Bar Harbor Story's photos (16 Apr 2025, 3 Jul 2024). The rail's extent and the stair's spot are ASSUMED until V5.1, V5.2.

Site 1 item 24 (docs/sites/bar-harbor-waterfront.md, stretch 5). Level metres. Faces, feet, tops: 2021 lidar (tools/assets/sites/wall_profile.py), pre-storm. Poured concrete as far as the VIA's Grant Park to Hancock Street job (2024-25, Bar Harbor Story 3 Jul 2024) is ASSUMED to reach, about (211, 1506); older granite south of it, ASSUMED until V5.3. Fence and stacked stones from Bar Harbor Story's photo (4 Apr 2024); its line is ASSUMED. Balance Rock: its place from two Waymarking listings and the lidar.

Site 1 item 26, stretch 1, survey 1.07-1.14: the Bar Harbor Regency's pier and floats. Level metres. Pier: traced on the raw lidar (ME_MidCoast 2021, tide -1.33): deck +3.92, rails +5.05, lamps +6.6, 48 x 3.6 m, its line 37.8 deg, not the +5.0 the survey first said (that was the rail). Built of: from marinas.com's undated aerials (before 2022: the truss bridges still stand), read as a small bridge on concrete portal bents, ASSUMED concrete and steel girders; bents at 10, 20.5, 31.6, 42 m from the top-down photo, scaled on the lidar's 48 m (11.2 px/m). Floats: absent from the lidar, so summer only. Gangway 9.5 m; stem 74 m with the photo's joints (21.4, 12.5, 40.2), the T head from chart SLCONS 544 and OSM 693638909 and the resort's own page ('T-shaped floating dock 200 feet in length and 140 feet across the top'): the T head is NOT in the aerials, so it came later. The comb and the small float at the stem's root are in the aerials; the small float is on the chart, the comb is not, so the comb is ASSUMED still there until V1.1.

Site 1 item 25, stretch 2, survey 2.02-2.04: the Atlantic Oceanside Hotel's pier, on the lidar's returns (ME_MidCoast 2021, flown at a tide of -1.34), not the chart's line, which lies 8 m west. Level metres. A 37 m walkway 2.4 m wide falling at 1:15 from +7.05 at the bank to +4.5, a 4 x 8 m head at +4.25 two steps down, a gangway of about 20 m, a float 5.3 x 31.5 m with a wing at its shore end (deck -0.7 at that tide: freeboard 0.64). Boats lay along both sides of the float in 2021; they are not part of this. The hotel's name for it, its timber or aluminium build and its colours wait on photo V2.2 (K6 timber, ASSUMED, as Maine's commonest). Whether the float comes in for the winter is unknown: summer_only ASSUMED, as the site's other private floats.

Site 1 item 25, stretch 2, survey row (no data): a private pier below the Bay View, in no chart, OSM or footprint data, found only in the lidar (ME_MidCoast 2021, tide -1.34). Level metres. 24.5 m x 2 m: 8 m falling at 1:4 from the bank (+6.1 to +4.1; a stair or cleated ramp, ASSUMED cleated ramp), then 16.5 m level at +4.1, rails +5.1; at the outer end something 3 m wide reaches +6.5 (a gallows for the gangway, ASSUMED: hoist); a gangway of about 15 m to a float, deck -0.8 at that tide (freeboard 0.55), about 5 m across the gangway's foot; its length along the shore is not in the returns (3 x 6 ASSUMED). All of it waits on photo V2.1.

K6 test and first use: the private pier off Ogden Point (survey 6.14/6.15, docs/sites/bar-harbor-waterfront.md stretch 6). Level metres. 41 m x 3 m, deck +4.3 NAVD; the lidar's ground falls from +1.6 at the root to -1.1 at the outer end (height_root_m 2.7, height_m 5.4 below the deck). The charted head 6.15 (6 x 7 m) is absent from the 2021 lidar, flown out of season: a seasonal float on a gangway (summer_only). Rails at +5.3 match the lidar's raised edges. Timber or aluminium waits on photo V6.2.

Site 1 item 26a, survey row 1.15a: the Bar Harbor Regency's terrace and shore walls at the pier's root. Level metres, built by tools/assets/sites/regency_terrace.py. Outlines and heights: 2021 lidar's ground returns. That it is granite block and riprap with a paved terrace and tables: marinas.com's undated aerials, as noted on 2 Nov (not re-read for this file; not in the repo). ASSUMED until V1.1: the wall's and paving's stone, no rail along the face (no returns), the wall hidden under trees NW of the pier, the steps at b 8 (the lidar shows only a 3 m ramp in the back wall), the number of tables.

Site 1 item 28, first slice: the remains of Dorr's saltwater pool at Compass Harbor, built by tools/assets/sites/compass_harbor.py. Positions are a reading of the 2021 lidar, ASSUMED until photo V7.2/V7.3; see the survey's stretch 7.

Site 1 item 30: the jointed ledges round the COA pier, K11, built by tools/assets/sites/coa_ledges.py from the 2021 lidar and Matt's 3 Nov photos. meta.solids on the dressing lists each block for a hull to strike.

Site 1 item 29b: the state's walls and rip-rap from the Regency to Bridge Street. Level metres, built by tools/assets/sites/west_street_north.py. That they exist: MGS Coastal Structure and Dune Crest Inventory. Lines, heights, which is wall and which rip-rap: 2021 lidar's ground returns. Stone, coping and colour ASSUMED until V1.1, V3.1, V3.2.

Site 1 item 28, second slice: the granite stair from the shore to Oldfarm, built by tools/assets/sites/oldfarm_steps.py from a 2015 photo; the line is the lidar's evenest, ASSUMED. See the survey's stretch 7.

Site 1 item 27, rows 1.16, 1.28-1.33: the ferry terminal as it stands since 2022. Built by tools/assets/sites/ferry_terminal.py from the 2021 lidar and GEI 2021. NOT built: the two truss bridges and the ramp building (removed 2022), the thin walkway and shed between the piers at about (-1950, 10)...(-1925, 38) (in the 2021 lidar, in no document; ASSUMED gone with them until V1.3), the turning dolphin (no returns; V1.4). The linkspan and pontoon are `linkspans` (item 19). Colours are the style's until V1.x, except the ramp's.

Site 1 item 29a: rip-rap on the private shore, Wayman Lane to Cromwell Cove. Level metres, built by tools/assets/sites/private_shore_riprap.py. That it is rip-rap: MGS Coastal Structure and Dune Crest Inventory. Lines and heights: 2021 lidar's ground returns. Stone size and colour ASSUMED until V5.6.

Site 1 item 30, twentieth slice: the town pier's parking lot, built by tools/assets/sites/town_pier_top.py from the two aerial photos. Drawn over structures.json's fill: paving, lines, cars. No cut in the ground.
